record.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe with multilingual speech tasks and public model artifacts
record.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe on October 28, 2026, with public model artifacts. Its model card and technical report describe an open-weight offline speech model supporting transcription in 40 languages and additional tasks including speaker attribution, translation and audio question answering. The report specifies BF16 weights and one H100 for its accuracy evaluations, and reports a 4.71% mean WER on nine public English Open ASR datasets. NVIDIA's launch article instead reports 5.33%; the discrepancy remains unexplained. These are company-reported results, not an independent reproduction. NVIDIA's fastest serving figure uses a separate implementation it says is not yet in the open-source release.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: NVIDIA published the Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe model card and release article on October 28, 2026, and made model artifacts available through its linked repositories.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: NVIDIA describes the open-weight offline model as supporting transcription across 40 languages, speaker-attributed transcription, speech translation, language identification and audio question answering, with recordings up to one hour; task and language support varies.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: NVIDIA's Oct 28 launch article reports a 5.33% English mean WER, while the current model card and Oct 28 technical report report 4.71%. The report defines its comparison as the nine-set public English Open ASR Leaderboard mean, using BF16 weights and lists baseline results from Oct 21, 2026. The source difference remains unexplained; this review did not independently reproduce either result.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Independent performance, reliable results across all listed languages and tasks, customer outcomes and production suitability are not established by this review.

contradictory_evidence.description: The NVIDIA-authored launch article reports 5.33% English mean WER, while the current official model card reports 4.71% and states that its results were captured October 12, 2026. The review did not determine whether this reflects different model revisions, benchmark snapshots or evaluation configurations.

evidence_gaps.description: NVIDIA's Oct 28 launch article reports 5.33% English mean WER, whereas its current model card and Oct 28 technical report report 4.71%. The report specifies a nine-set public leaderboard mean using BF16 weights and Oct 21 baselines but does not explain the launch-article difference.
The reported benchmark results have not been independently reproduced in this review.
The model card says task and language support varies; audio understanding and spoken instruction following were evaluated only in English.

brief.importance_rationale: If the documented release scope holds, an openly available model that combines multilingual transcription, speaker attribution, translation, language identification and audio question answering, with public model artifacts and a reusable data-curation release, expands the tools available to speech researchers and developers. The consequence is meaningful but bounded: provider-reported benchmark results are not independently reproduced, support varies by task and language, and optimized serving figures use a separate implementation not yet in the open-source release.
limitations: Benchmark results are NVIDIA-reported and were not independently reproduced.

The Oct 28 launch article reports 5.33% English mean WER, while the live model card and technical report report 4.71%; the report specifies a nine-set public-board mean using BF16 weights but does not explain the article's different value.
Task and language support varies; the model card says audio understanding and spoken instruction following were evaluated only in English.
NVIDIA says the optimized serving implementation underlying its fastest throughput figures is not yet part of the open-source release.
This activation did not run inference, audit the full benchmark protocols, inspect the entire data manifest or review the license terms.

The report specifies BF16 weights and one H100 for its accuracy evaluations, and reports a 4.71% mean WER on nine public English Open ASR datasets. NVIDIA's launch article instead reports 5.33%; the discrepancy remains unexplained. These are company-reported results, not an independent reproduction. NVIDIA's fastest serving figure uses a separate implementation it says is not yet in the open-source release.

technical.claimed_result: NVIDIA reports 4.71% mean WER on nine public English Open ASR datasets in its Oct 28 technical report, using BF16 weights; the report lists baseline results from the Oct 21 leaderboard. Its launch article reports 5.33% English mean WER. The source difference remains unexplained, and no result was independently reproduced here.
technical.demonstrated_result: The October 28 release article, model card and linked public model artifacts are observable. This activation did not run model inference or reproduce benchmark results.
technical.mechanism: The model card describes a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts language backbone with audio and speaker encoders for speech-to-text tasks.
technical.regime: NVIDIA describes an offline model supporting recordings up to one hour, with language and task support varying across the stated functions.
technical.reproducibility: The model card gives deployment instructions and links to artifacts. This activation did not pin artifact revisions, audit benchmark protocols, inspect the full data manifest or run inference.
technical.strongest_baseline: The report lists open-weight and commercial systems from the Oct 21 leaderboard. The published 4.71% mean is below listed open-weight baselines and above several commercial-system means; the results are NVIDIA-reported and were not independently reproduced in this review.

brief.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe with multilingual speech tasks and public model artifacts
brief.why_it_matters: A publicly available model that combines several speech tasks with multilingual support can broaden the options for speech research and applications. The release establishes availability and NVIDIA's stated design; benchmark performance, broad language quality and real deployment impact remain unverified.
